etymology: Pictograph of a great ceremonial axe, emblem of royal power; the classic reading sees three lines (heaven, humankind, earth) joined by one vertical: the king.
mnemonic: Heaven, people, earth — and one stroke holding all three together: that job is the king's — オウ.

etymology: Pictograph: a cowrie shell with its feelers — cowries were ancient China's money, so 貝 marks value in 買, 貸, 質 and kin.
mnemonic: A shell on two little legs — かい. Wherever 貝 hides in a kanji, money is changing hands.

etymology: Pictograph: three jade discs strung on a cord; the dot was added to distinguish it from 王 'king'.
mnemonic: The king (王) with one gem in his pocket — たま. Jade beads, rice balls, ten-yen coins: anything round and precious.

etymology: Pictograph: a twisted skein of silk. As a left-side component it spins through everything woven, tied or connected (紙, 線, 組).
mnemonic: A silk skein with loose ends dangling — いと. Follow the thread and half the kanji dictionary unravels.

etymology: Pictograph: a boulder (口) lying at the foot of a cliff (厂) — stone.
mnemonic: One rock rolled off the cliff and sat down at the bottom — いし. It's been there since the oracle bones.

etymology: Phono-semantic: plants (艹) + 早 'early' (phonetic ソウ) — the green that comes up earliest and everywhere: grass.
mnemonic: Up at dawn (早) before anything else in the garden: the weeds — くさ. Grass never sleeps in.

etymology: Pictograph: two bamboo stalks with drooping leaves. As a crown (⺮) it heads everything once made of bamboo: brushes, boxes, flutes, counting slips.
mnemonic: Two stalks leaning together, leaves like little flags — たけ. Under the bamboo crown, someone is always weaving or counting.

etymology: Pictograph: originally a coiled viper; the sign broadened to cover every creeping, crawling creature: insects.
mnemonic: A grub standing upright with feelers out — むし. The kanji started as a snake and got demoted to bugs.

etymology: Pictograph: a pair of wings, each with its barbs — feathers; the counter for birds and rabbits.
mnemonic: Two wings folded side by side — はね. Rabbits get counted with it too: monks once declared them 'birds' to eat them.

etymology: 云 alone was the original cloud pictograph — curling vapor; the rain crown (雨) was added once 云 got borrowed for 'to say'.
mnemonic: Vapor curling up (云) until the sky's ceiling (雨) catches it — くも. A cloud is rain still making up its mind.

etymology: Phono-semantic: walls (囗) + 袁 (phonetic エン) — a walled pleasure-ground: garden, park.
mnemonic: Trailing robes strolling inside the walls: the palace garden — その, エン. 公園 opened those walls to everyone; 動物園 filled them with animals.

etymology: Origin debated — most read the old form as a person wearing a great jade pendant at the belt; it has meant 'yellow' since the oracle bones.
mnemonic: A courtier weighed down by an amber pendant, glowing at the waist — きいろ. Yellow is the color of worn treasure.

etymology: Compound ideograph: grain (禾) sorted with the measuring ladle (斗) — grading into kinds: category, department, branch of study.
mnemonic: Scoop the harvest into bins: this grade here, that grade there — カ. 科学 sorts the world; 歯科 is the tooth bin.

etymology: Simplified from 繪: threads (糸) brought together (会) — colored silks meeting in embroidery: a picture.
mnemonic: Where the colored threads all meet (会), an image appears — え. Before paint, pictures were sewn.

etymology: Pictograph: an animal horn with its striations — a horn; hence anything that juts: angle, corner.
mnemonic: A striped horn planted point-up — つの; turn at it and it's the かど, the street corner; measure it and it's カク, the angle.

etymology: Phono-semantic: water (氵) + a phonetic written 舌 — water rushing and gurgling: alive, vigorous.
mnemonic: A stream chattering like a tongue (舌): that sound is aliveness — カツ. 生活 is your daily portion of it.

etymology: Pictograph: a person curled into a ball mid-tumble — round, whole.
mnemonic: Knees to chin, rolling downhill — まる. Ships and castle keeps take it as a name-ending: the 〜丸, snug and complete.

etymology: Compound ideograph: mountain (山) + stone (石) — mountain-sized stone: a boulder, bedrock.
mnemonic: A stone with a whole mountain stacked on top — いわ. Not a pebble: the kind climbers rope onto.

etymology: Phono-semantic: words (言) + 己 (phonetic キ) — words set down so the self won't forget: to record.
mnemonic: Write it down (言) for your future self (己) — キ. 日記 is that deal kept nightly; the 記者 keeps it for everyone.

etymology: Phono-semantic: 开 'frame' (phonetic ケイ) + 彡 'strokes of shading' — the outline plus its rendering: shape, form.
mnemonic: First the frame, then three quick shading strokes: the form appears — かたち. Every 人形 (doll) is born this way.

etymology: Compound ideograph: a spring (泉) welling at the foot of a cliff (厂) — the source; and the open land it waters: plain, meadow; hence 'original'.
mnemonic: Where the water first leaves the rock: the source — はら, the open field it feeds; ゲン, the origin of things (原因).

etymology: Pictograph: a single door leaf on its hinge — half of the double gate 門: the household door, and the counter for households.
mnemonic: One door leaf, slightly ajar — と. A 門 is for the city; a 戸 is for your house. 江戸: the door of the bay.

etymology: Pictograph: a person standing with legs crossed — crossing, exchanging, mingling.
mnemonic: Legs crossed mid-dance-step: paths crossing everywhere — まじわる. 交通 is a whole city doing it at once.

etymology: Compound ideograph, by the classic account: to divide (八) away the private (厶) — what belongs to no one alone: public.
mnemonic: Split open the private pocket and share it out: public property — コウ. The 公園 is the garden nobody owns and everybody has.

etymology: Pictograph read as a new sprout breaking the ground — raw, inborn capacity: talent; borrowed in Japanese as the everyday counter for age.
mnemonic: One shoot up before the field is even plowed: born gifted — サイ. Age borrowed the character: 十才, ten years grown.

etymology: Phono-semantic: thread (糸) + a right side originally the fontanelle 囟 (later written 田) — thread fine as a baby's hair: thin, detailed.
mnemonic: Thread split until it's almost thought — ほそい. 細かい is that fineness applied to details (and to people who mind them).

etymology: Compound ideograph: hands (廾) working bamboo counting-rods (竹) on the board — to calculate.
mnemonic: Bamboo rods clicking between busy hands: ancient spreadsheet — サン. 計算 still means moving the rods, just faster.

etymology: Originally 'to hold, administer' (a foot + a hand): a government office; when Buddhism arrived, the office that housed foreign monks became the temple.
mnemonic: The old administration building handed over to the monks — てら. It still administrates: bells, time, and half the kanji it appears in (時, 待, 持).

etymology: Simplified from 數: a hand with a stick (攵) tallying off a bundled phonetic — to count; a number.
mnemonic: Tap, tap, tap — the stick counts the sacks of rice — かず, スウ. 数学 is the tapping turned into a science.

etymology: Phono-semantic: sun (日) + 生 (phonetic セイ) — lights born (生) of the same fire as the sun, scattered small: stars.
mnemonic: Baby suns sprouting (生) across the night field — ほし. Each star is the sun's seedling.

etymology: Phono-semantic: sun (日) + 青 'blue' (phonetic セイ) — the sun in a blue sky: clear weather.
mnemonic: Sun plus blue: the forecast you wanted — はれ. 晴れ is the sky wearing its best kanji.

etymology: Compound ideograph: rain (雨) + a hand with a broom (彗 reduced to ヨ) — the one precipitation you have to sweep: snow.
mnemonic: Rain you shovel — ゆき. The broom under the rain-crown is the whole story of a northern winter.

etymology: Phono-semantic: thread (糸) + 泉 'spring' (phonetic セン) — a thread flowing continuous as spring-water: a line.
mnemonic: Water from the spring pulled into a thread that never breaks — セン. Train lines (山手線), phone lines, pencil lines: all this thread.

etymology: Phono-semantic: boat (舟) + 㕣 (phonetic セン) — the full-sized vessel: a ship.
mnemonic: The little boat (舟) that grew a cabin and a cargo hold — ふね. 風船 is its airborne cousin: a balloon, ship of wind.

etymology: Phono-semantic: thread (糸) + 且 (phonetic ソ) — cords braided together: to assemble; the group so woven.
mnemonic: Strands braided into one rope: the team — くみ. 組み立てる is braiding parts into a machine; a 番組 braids minutes into a show.

etymology: Pictograph: slopes parting above a mouth-like opening — the cleft where water exits the mountains: a valley.
mnemonic: Two ridges peel apart and the land opens its mouth — たに. 渋谷: the valley that got a scramble crossing.

etymology: Compound ideograph: ten (十) eyes (目) inspecting even the hidden corner (乚) — nothing crooked survives: straight, honest; to set straight.
mnemonic: Ten eyes check the corner and the line comes out true — なおす, to fix; ただちに, straight away. Honesty is just geometry with witnesses.

etymology: Simplified from 點 'black mark': 占 (phonetic テン) over fire (灬) — a burn-black dot: a point, a mark, a score.
mnemonic: The fortune-teller (占) drops sparks (灬) — each scorch mark one point — テン. Tests are scored in little burns: 百点!

etymology: Simplified from 當: 尚 (phonetic トウ) over 田 — fields matched in value: fitting exactly; hence to hit the mark, to be right.
mnemonic: The dart lands dead on — あたる. 当たり! for the winning ticket; 本当 for the statement that hits reality square.

etymology: Compound ideograph: entering (入) under a cover (冂) — what is within: inside.
mnemonic: Step in under the tent flap: now you're in-house — うち. 家内, 案内, 内緒: family, guidance, secrets — all indoor matters.

etymology: Pictograph: a horse — arched neck with mane (the top strokes) and four galloping legs flattened into dots (灬).
mnemonic: Mane flying, four hooves drumming into dots — うま. Stations (駅) and tests (験) still carry this horse inside them.

etymology: Simplified from 麥: the wheat plant (來) with a foot (夂) below — grain trodden into the winter field: barley, wheat.
mnemonic: Stamp the seed in and let winter do the rest — むぎ. Beer, udon and bread all start at this footprint.

etymology: Compound ideograph: an animal's paw-print (釆) crossing a field (田) — tracks in sequence: one's turn, a number in a series.
mnemonic: Prints across the paddy, one after another: whose turn is it? — バン. 一番 is the first footprint; 電話番号 a whole trail of them.

etymology: Pictograph: rice grains spreading from the ear of the plant. Also abbreviates アメリカ (米国) by old phonetic convention.
mnemonic: Six grains bursting off the stalk — こめ. One kanji feeds a continent and names another: 米国, the rice-character country that grows wheat.

etymology: Compound ideograph: mouth (口) + bird (鳥) — the bird's voice: to cry, chirp; of things, to ring and sound.
mnemonic: Give the bird its mouth back and the morning starts — なく. Phones, bells and stomachs all 鳴る: everything chirps in Japanese.

etymology: Pictograph: a tuft of hair curling at the tip — fur, hair, down.
mnemonic: One curling hair, magnified — け. 毛布 is a blanket of it; the 髪の毛 on your head is this kanji by the hundred thousand.

etymology: Compound ideograph: grain (禾) bending supple over a woman (女) — to bend to another's will: to entrust, delegate.
mnemonic: Hand your harvest over and let someone else carry it — イ. A 委員会 is a room of people holding everyone else's grain.

etymology: Compound ideograph: a child head-down at birth (𠫓) over flesh (月) — the newborn fed and grown: to raise, to be raised.
mnemonic: From the first upside-down cry, feeding flesh onto tiny bones — そだてる. 教育 raises the mind the same way.

etymology: Phono-semantic: water (氵) + 永 'long, eternal' (phonetic エイ) — long strokes drawn through water: to swim.
mnemonic: Stretch each stroke as long as forever (永) — およぐ. 水泳: eternity practiced in a 25-meter pool.
